findings.title: Google Meet booking with no destination calendar throws a TypeError in `EventManager.create`
findings.description: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when there is no destination, and line 119 reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no `?.`. That read runs whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType` (`"integrations:google:meet"`, packages/app-store/locations.ts:54). handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 sets `destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination, and handleNewBooking.ts:2114 calls `eventManager.create(evt)` on the normal path. The old line was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was null-safe, and the comment on line 116 describes exactly this fallback case. The TypeError is thrown before any calendar or video event is created, so the booking fails.

findings.title: Organization slug is written under an inverted billing condition
findings.description: The original `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` wrote `slug` when billing was disabled. The new `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` writes it only when billing is enabled. The `requestedSlug` on line 153 kept its original polarity (`IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? {...} : {}`). So with billing disabled the organization is created with neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug`. With billing enabled, the slug is written directly, bypassing the requested-slug flow.

findings.title: Video booking references are saved without `credentialId`, so cancellation never deletes the meeting
findings.description: The line `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` replaces the former `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. Video results from `createMeeting` carry `credentialId: credential.id` (packages/core/videoClient.ts:78), but `isCalendarType` is false for them (`result.type.includes("_calendar")`), so the value is dropped. `referencesToCreate` is persisted as-is (handleNewBooking.ts:2367-2369). handleCancelBooking.ts:491 calls `deleteMeeting` only when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is truthy, so cancelled bookings with a dedicated video link keep their meeting.

findings.title: Legacy destinations without `credentialId` create Google events in "primary" instead of the selected calendar
findings.description: `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable (packages/prisma/schema.prisma:159). For such rows, `createAllCalendarEvents` (packages/core/EventManager.ts:375-381) calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the destination's `externalId`. `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent` picks the calendar with `find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, which can never match a null `credentialId`, so `calendarId` becomes `"primary"` on line 154. The previous code used `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. The stored reference also has no `externalCalendarId` (EventManager.ts:169 reads `result.externalId`, which is undefined on this path), which feeds the next finding. The hangout-link `calendar.events.patch` at lines 166-168 still uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which is now possibly undefined, and its promise is not awaited or handled.

findings.title: Google delete and update fallback lookup compares `externalId` against the falsy `externalCalendarId`, so it never finds the destination
findings.description: `deleteEvent` computes `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. In that else branch `externalCalendarId` is null, undefined, or empty, and destination `externalId`s are non-null strings, so the `find` always returns undefined. Line 322 then deletes from `"primary"`, and a 404 is resolved silently (line 335). For a cancelled booking whose reference has no `externalCalendarId` (the pre-refactor else branch at handleCancelBooking.ts:473-482, or the references from the previous finding), the event stays on the user's selected calendar while the cancel reports success. The original code was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. The same expression in `updateEvent` (lines 254-256) makes `calendarId` undefined at line 261.

findings.title: Office365 `createEvent` always targets `destinationCalendar[0]`, ignoring the credential it is invoked for
findings.description: `CalendarManager.createEvent` accepts the per-destination `externalId` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:221) and echoes it in the result (line 267), but never passes it to `calendar.createEvent` (line 236, which gets only `credential.id`). Office365 then posts to `/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId}/events`, the first destination. For COLLECTIVE events, handleNewBooking.ts:1077-1079 appends team members' destinations, so a member's Office365 credential posts to the organizer's calendar id. That request fails, and CalendarManager logs it and drops the result. Lark (larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128-129) uses the same first-destination selection. In CalDAV (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-165), the filter matches no calendar, `responses` is empty, and the method still returns a success object (lines 185-192), so the event is silently not written.

findings.title: Collective team members' calendars are silently dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
findings.description: When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (lines 1063-1067). Member destinations are collected at lines 992-993, but they are appended with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` on line 1078, which is a no-op when the value is null. The collective event is therefore not written to members' calendars, and no error is raised.

findings.title: `updateAllCalendarEvents` catch block no longer logs the error
findings.description: The diff removes `console.error(message)` from this catch. The `message` string is still built at lines 592-595 but never used. Failures from the Prisma lookups (lines 485, 517, 557), `getCalendar`, and `deleteEvent` are converted into `success: false` results with no log, where they were previously logged.

findings.title: An empty dynamic user list is reported as HTTP 500, and the validation message is discarded
findings.description: `throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` runs inside the `try` that starts at line 725. The catch at lines 757-761 rethrows only `HttpError` and `PrismaClientKnownRequestError` (as 400). Any other error becomes `HttpError 500 "Unable to load users"`. A dynamic-group request whose user list is empty therefore gets a server error, and the explicit validation message never reaches the caller.
